extracted.intended_audience: advanced postdoctoral researchers and clinician‑scientists (and institutional grants administrators) preparing K99/R00 Career Transition Award applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an NIH Career Transition (K99/R00) award application, including eligibility (organization and PD/PI), required materials, parent announcement usage, and administrative procedures. Targets the mentored K99 phase helping postdocs transition to independent investigator positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Purpose / Intended Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: To support the initial phase of a Career/Research Transition award program that provides 1-2 years of mentored support for highly motivated, advanced postdoctoral research scientists. The program is designed to facilitate a timely transition of outstanding postdoctoral researchers or clinician-scientists from mentored research positions to independent, tenure-track or equivalent faculty positions, and to provide independent NIH research support during the transition that will help these individuals launch competitive, independent research careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this statement to demonstrate alignment/fit in the application narrative — the award is explicitly for transitioning postdocs to independent investigators and provides mentored support (typically 1–2 years) followed by independent support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully read the Eligibility section of the specific funding opportunity for opportunity-specific organization eligibility requirements — the parent page cautions that there may be additional or differing organization eligibility rules per funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI Eligibility — citizenship and career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PI U.S. Citizenship Requirement: No. Career Stage: Postdoctorate/Residency, Early Career. U.S. citizen or non-citizen, with research or clinical doctoral degree, and no more than 4 years of Post-Doctoral research experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm your exact career-stage calculation and any opportunity-specific PD/PI eligibility rules in the funding opportunity. The page emphasizes careful reading of the opportunity-specific PD/PI eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored Phase Requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The K99 includes a mentored phase (K99); applications should propose and justify mentored training and mentorship plans appropriate for transitioning the candidate to independence. Use the mentoring plan and mentoring letter content to reflect the mentored nature of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Letters Requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the required number of reference letters (at least 3, no more than 5). Ensure letters address the candidate's potential for transition to independence and other evaluation-pertinent topics as specified in the funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Instrument and Category
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding Instrument: Grant. Funding Category: Research Training and Career Development. Budget Mechanism Code: OR - Other Research Related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These designations determine administrative routing, allowable budget elements, and review/tooling. Prepare the application using grant forms and budget items appropriate for a Research Training/Career Development award and the specified budget mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Parent Announcements (K99/R00)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent Announcements K99/R00 are available. Parent announcements are broad funding opportunities that applicants can use to submit investigator-initiated applications for a range of popular programs. They do not specify any particular area of scientific interest. They simply provide the standard forms and instructions needed to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all NIH institutes and centers participate on all parent announcements. Check the participating organization in the funding opportunity before applying. After identifying a funding opportunity, follow the parent announcement and any opportunity‑specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Submission — Follow the How to Apply Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: After identifying a funding opportunity, follow guidance in the How to Apply – Application Guide including any Career Development (K) instruction call-outs, except where instructed to do otherwise in the funding opportunity or related notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Application Guide's K-specific call-outs for formatting, page limits, required components (e.g., candidate/career development plan, mentor statements, institutional commitment). If the funding opportunity or notices override the Guide, follow those instructions instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating Funding Organizations and Mission Fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must fit within the mission of at least one participating funding organization and meet all opportunity-specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before applying, verify which NIH institutes/centers participate in the specific opportunity (the page lists many participating organizations). Craft aims and significance to align with at least one participating organization's mission and any institute-specific priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due Dates, Review, and Award Cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Key Dates section of funding opportunities lists specific due dates. Many opportunities indicate Standard Due Dates apply. Review and Award Cycles include New, Renewal, Resubmission, Revision as Allowed; Scientific Merit Review; Advisory Council Review; Earliest Start Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Key Dates for the specific opportunity and plan submission timelines accordingly. Be aware of the review and award cycle stages and any deadlines for resubmission/renewal. Adhere strictly to stated due dates and cycles in the opportunity announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIDS and AIDS‑Related Applications Policy Note
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with applications for Advisory Council Review in January 2027 (i.e., application due dates on or after May 25, 2026), NIH will no longer accept applications submitted on dedicated AIDS application due dates. (NOT-OD-26-029)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your application is AIDS- or AIDS‑related, check the notice and adjust submission planning; do not rely on dedicated AIDS application due dates for submissions on/after the specified dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Staff Roles and Contacts / Post‑Submission Tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you apply, check your chosen funding opportunity for application submission, scientific/research, peer review, and financial/grants management contacts. After you apply, find NIH staff assignments in the Status module of eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage institutional sponsored programs/grants administrators for internal and agency policy questions. Use the listed NIH contacts for pre-submission questions and eRA Commons to track staff assignments and application status after submission.
